blocks.text: Why you need to troubleshoot podcast RSS feed errors

Your RSS feed is the heartbeat of your show. When it breaks, your new episodes fail to reach listening apps like Apple Podcasts or Spotify. This creates a disconnect with your audience. Most errors are simple syntax issues. They occur when an invalid character sneaks into your show notes or title. Sometimes, a hosting platform update changes your URL structure without notice. You do not need to be a developer to fix this. You just need a systematic approach to identify the broken tag.
Common causes of RSS feed failures

Most feed issues are human errors. You might have pasted a special character like a smart quote into your description. XML files are strict. A single unescaped ampersand will break the entire feed. Another common cause is a missing enclosure tag. If your audio file is not properly linked, the player cannot download it. Check your hosting platform dashboard first. Many providers include an automatic validator. If that fails, copy your feed URL into a third party validator tool.
How to fix your feed without buying tools

items: Open your RSS feed URL in Safari or Chrome to see the raw XML code.
Use ⌘ + F to search for common problematic characters like & or unclosed tags.
Check your show notes for hidden formatting characters that might have carried over from Google Docs.
Verify your image dimensions match the requirements for Apple Podcasts to avoid validation warnings.
Ensure your audio file hosting link remains active and public.

blocks.text: Using your Mac to manage feed health

Your Mac is an excellent tool for deep technical work. If you need to edit your feed manually, avoid word processors. Use a plain text editor like TextEdit or BBEdit. This ensures no hidden formatting is added to your XML. Keep your show notes in a clean format before you export them to your host. If you manage multiple shows, keep a local archive of your past feed versions. This helps you compare changes if a new episode causes a sudden spike in errors.

If you are stuck on a specific error message, ask Lazur to explain the XML tag requirements. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and point at the error on your screen to get a clear, spoken answer about what the validator is seeing.
blocks.title: Get instant technical help

blocks.text: The best way to handle technical issues is to avoid them entirely. Develop a strict checklist for every episode. Validate your feed every time you update your show notes. If you use a CMS, check for plugins that might be altering your feed structure. Test your feed in a sandbox environment if your host provides one. Consistency is your best defense against technical errors.

faq.question: How do I know if my podcast RSS feed is broken?
faq.answer: If your latest episode does not appear in Apple Podcasts or Spotify within a few hours, check your feed in a validator tool. These tools will highlight the exact line of code that is failing.

faq.question: Can I fix RSS errors without knowing how to code?
faq.answer: Yes. Most errors are caused by simple text characters. You just need to remove or escape the invalid character. Validators usually point out the exact line and character causing the problem.

faq.question: Does my hosting platform keep my feed valid automatically?
faq.answer: Most do, but they cannot prevent errors caused by your own input. If you paste text with special symbols into your episode description, you might break the feed regardless of your platform.
